name: Off-Road Vehicle
description: Any motorized vehicle designed for or capable of cross-country travel over natural terrain and not intended for use mainly on public roads, explicitly including two-wheel vehicles powered by any source but muscle or wind, so an electric dirt bike built for off-road use falls here. No limit on power or speed.

restrictions.rule: Designed for or capable of cross-country travel over land or other natural terrain, and not intended for use mainly on public roads; two-wheel vehicles and any power source other than muscle or wind are included (O.C.G.A. §40-7-3)
No limit on motor power or speed (O.C.G.A. §40-7-3)
Must have operative brakes and a muffler or other silencing equipment (O.C.G.A. §40-7-4)
Not allowed on private property without the owner's or agent's express written permission (O.C.G.A. §40-7-4)
Not allowed in a perennial stream except to cross it directly (O.C.G.A. §40-7-4)
Cities and counties may set times and zones of use by ordinance, and state agencies on the land they manage (O.C.G.A. §40-7-5)
A violation is a civil penalty of at least $25, not a crime (O.C.G.A. §40-7-6)
The Act sets no registration, sticker, license, age, helmet or safety-course requirement (O.C.G.A. §§40-7-1 through 40-7-6)
Georgia issues no title for a vehicle not sold for lawful highway use
Ridden on a public road, a two-wheeled one is a motorcycle and needs registration and a Class M license
